extra.message: User-controlled URL (extracted from req.body.content via regex) is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to exec('identify ' + url). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary OS commands.

User-supplied req.body.password (and username) are passed directly into User.find({}). When a JSON body is sent, password can be an object like {"$gt": ""} which bypasses authentication, enabling NoSQL injection / authentication bypass.

extra.message: _.merge(message, req.body.message, {...}) merges attacker-controlled JSON into a new object. lodash 4.17.4 _.merge is vulnerable to prototype pollution; sending {"__proto__": {"canDelete": true}} pollutes Object.prototype and grants delete privileges, bypassing access control.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: res.redirect(redirectPage) redirects to a user-controlled value (req.body.redirectPage). An attacker can craft a login request that redirects the victim to an arbitrary external URL, enabling phishing.

extra.message: Todo content is user-controlled (stored via POST /create) and rendered with unescaped <%- marked(...) %>. marked 0.3.5's sanitize:true option does not reliably prevent HTML/JS injection, allowing stored XSS.
